items.question: According to Section 4.1, what must be done each time an operating limitation is exceeded?
options: Record in the logbook with limit exceeded, duration, extreme value, and additional info
Only reset the system and continue flight
items.explanation: The manual requires an entry in the logbook each time a limitation is exceeded, including details of the event.

items.question: What must be checked to ensure proper weight and balance of the AS350 B3 before flight?
options: Weight of fuel, oil, payload, CG, and that limits in Section 2 are not exceeded
items.explanation: Proper weight and balance requires checking all fluids, payload, and CG against limitations.

items.question: What should be ensured before starting preflight checks in the AS350 B3?
options: All corrective maintenance operations for flightworthiness are performed
items.explanation: The manual specifies that all corrective maintenance required for flightworthiness must be completed before preflight.

items.question: If the AS350 B3 helicopter has been parked for more than 2 days, what is required during preflight check?
items.explanation: After 2 days or in case of visible leak/doubt, cowls must be opened during preflight.

items.question: During exterior preflight check, what must be confirmed regarding the MGB oil cooler air inlet?
options: Check that oil quantity is within limits
Ensure no obstruction or foreign objects
items.explanation: The MGB oil cooler air inlet must be free of obstructions or foreign objects.

items.question: What warning is given in the AS350 B3 manual about ice or snow around the engine air intake?
options: It may cause sudden in-flight engine failure
It will cause higher fuel burn
It will cause VEMD display malfunction
items.explanation: Ice or snow can be ingested and cause sudden in-flight engine failure.

items.question: What must be confirmed about the ELT during preflight check?
items.explanation: The ELT must be checked in the ARMED position.

items.question: What is required to check at the oil drain during preflight?
options: No oil is present under scupper
items.explanation: There should be no oil under the scupper during the oil drain check.

items.question: During turnaround check, what must be visually inspected for no impact damage?
items.explanation: Main and tail rotor blades must be inspected visually for no impact damage.

items.question: If the aircraft is parked between flights in winds above 40 kt (74 km/h), what is recommended?
options: Fit blanks, covers and blade socks
items.explanation: Temporary picketing with blanks, covers and blade socks is recommended in high winds.

items.question: What is the correct position of the rotor brake before engine start in the AS350 B3?
items.explanation: The rotor brake must be released and fully forward before engine start.

items.question: What must be the position of the fuel shut-off lever during engine prestart check?
options: FORWARD, with plastic guard in place
items.explanation: The fuel shut-off lever must be in the forward position with the guard in place.

items.question: What must be the position of the twist grip during engine prestart check?
items.explanation: The twist grip must be in IDLE position.

items.question: What should be checked about the [MASTER SW] or [EMER SW] during engine prestart?
items.explanation: The [MASTER SW] or [EMER SW] must be checked in the UP position.

items.question: What must be the position of the engine starting selector before start?
items.explanation: The engine starting selector must be set to OFF before engine start.

items.question: What is required for lighting circuits 1 and 2 before flight if night flight is intended?
items.explanation: Lighting circuits 1 and 2 must be tested (PERFORM) if night flight is planned.

items.question: What must be checked with the [FIRE TEST] during engine prestart?
items.explanation: The [FIRE TEST] ensures the fire detection and warning systems are functional.

items.question: What is checked on the VEMD during prestart?
options: Battery voltage > 22V, fuel quantity, bleed valve open, no fault messages
items.explanation: The VEMD check must confirm battery > 22V, correct fuel quantity, bleed valve open, and no fault messages.

items.question: During control checks, how should the cyclic be set?
items.explanation: The cyclic must be set in CENTER with friction adjusted.

items.question: During control checks, how should the collective be set?
items.explanation: The collective must be set to LOCK with friction adjusted.

items.question: What must be the status of heating, demisting, and air conditioning during prestart check?
items.explanation: Heating, demisting and air conditioning must be OFF during prestart.

items.question: During engine start, what must be checked on the CWP?
items.explanation: Engine Starting calls to CHECK CWP: GOV.

items.question: When must the [FUEL PUMP] be set to ON during engine start?
items.explanation: Step 2: [FUEL PUMP] (or [FUEL P]) — ON prior to start.

items.question: Which parameters must be monitored during engine start?
options: Ng increases; T4 remains within limits; rotor turns at Ng ≤ 25%; engine oil pressure increases
items.explanation: Checklist lists these four indications during start.

items.question: When Ng > 67%, which CWP lights must be checked?
items.explanation: At Ng ≥ 67% the CWP must show ENG P, MGB P, HYDR.

items.question: When should [PITOT] be set to ON during the start sequence?
options: After engine is running and CWP check completed
items.explanation: Sequence shows [PITOT] — ON after start and CWP checks.

items.question: At Ng > 60%, what happens on the VEMD upper screen?
options: It automatically switches to FLI display
items.explanation: NOTE 3: upper screen automatically switches to FLI display when Ng > 60%.

items.question: If EPU was used for start, what must be done after engine start?
options: Disconnect and ensure the EPU door is closed and locked
Leave EPU door open for cooling
items.explanation: Step 12: EPU (if used) — DISCONNECT; make sure EPU door is closed and locked.

items.question: During hydraulic accumulator checks, what must be verified on the collective?
items.explanation: Run-Up Check: Collective — CHECK correctly locked.

items.question: What CWP indication occurs when [HYD TEST] or [ACCU TST] is set to ON?
items.explanation: CWP — CHECK HYDR flashes during the accumulator test.

items.question: How is accumulator hydraulic assistance on pitch and roll checked?
options: Move cyclic to full deflection and hold
Move cyclic 2–3 times each axis (±10% travel) and check for normal feel/no abnormal loads
items.explanation: Move cyclic 2–3 times each axis (±10%) and verify normal control feel.

items.question: During the Hydraulic pressure isolation check, what is the correct sequence for the hydraulic cut-off switch (collective)?
items.explanation: Isolation check: cut-off OFF to feel loads, then back ON.

items.question: After the hydraulic cut-off is returned to ON, what HYDR light timing is acceptable?
items.explanation: CWP — CHECK HYDR after 3 to 4 sec; if reduced to 1 sec, maintenance is required.

items.question: At what NR must the horn audio warning be ON?
items.explanation: HORN — ON for NR < 360 rpm; OFF for NR > 360 rpm.

items.question: What must be confirmed when performing the [FIRE/TEST] during run-up?
options: ENG FIRE light and gong sound
items.explanation: FIRE/TEST — CHECK: ENG FIRE + Gong sounds.

items.question: What is the maximum duration for [CRANK] during the cranking procedure?
items.explanation: CRANK — PRESS for 30 sec max.

items.question: During cranking, what is the required position of the emergency fuel shut-off lever?
items.explanation: Emergency fuel shut-off lever — FORWARD.

items.question: What Ng value must be ensured during cranking?
items.explanation: Ng — CHECK ≤ 10%.

items.question: Why must the engine not be cranked with the emergency fuel shutoff closed or the fuel pump OFF?
options: It may damage the engine high pressure fuel pump
It may cause a hydraulic system fault
items.explanation: CAUTION: This could damage the high pressure fuel pump.

items.question: Before takeoff, what is the required door status?
options: Closed or sliding doors OPEN LOCKED
items.explanation: BEFORE TAKEOFF CHECK: Doors — CLOSED or sliding doors OPEN LOCKED.

items.question: Before takeoff, what must be the status of temperatures and pressures?
items.explanation: Temperatures and pressures — NORMAL RANGE.

items.question: Before takeoff, what must be the status of the CWP lights?
items.explanation: CWP — All lights OFF.

items.question: Before takeoff, what must be the status of the collective?
items.explanation: Collective — UNLOCKED.

items.question: During takeoff, what is prohibited above engine maximum continuous rating (Ng or T4)?
items.explanation: CAUTION: Use of heating and demisting is forbidden above maximum continuous rating.

items.question: What hover height is used for the initial takeoff check?
items.explanation: Procedure: Hover at 5 ft (1.5 m) to check engine and mechanical parameters.

items.question: In the takeoff profile, what is the minimum IAS at 40 ft (12 m)?
items.explanation: Climb to clear 40 ft with IAS = 50 kt (93 km/h).

items.question: For safe operation, what must be avoided in the takeoff path?
items.explanation: CAUTION: The takeoff path should avoid the HV diagram.

items.question: For maximum climb performance above 100 ft, what speed should be used?
items.explanation: Section 4.5 states Vy = IAS 65 kt at 0 Hp (-1 kt/1000 ft).

items.question: What defines fast cruise during normal operations?
options: The first limit reached in the FLI amber area
items.explanation: Fast cruise is obtained by the first limitation in the FLI amber area.

items.question: When may servo-transparency be reached?
options: At low torque with high speed
At Vy with low gross weight
items.explanation: Section 4.5 notes servo-transparency may occur in maneuvers near VNE.

items.question: What is the maximum rate for hover turns?
items.explanation: Avoid rotation faster than 6 sec per full rotation.

items.question: What action should be taken when flying in turbulence?
items.explanation: Section 4.5 states reduce IAS in turbulence.

items.question: At what speed should approach be initiated?
items.explanation: Begin approach at Vy.

items.question: At approximately 100 ft during approach, what must be done?
options: Reduce IAS to HIGE at 5 ft
items.explanation: At 100 ft reduce IAS down to HIGE at 5 ft.

items.question: What is the checklist item for landing light in approach?
items.explanation: Landing light = AS REQUIRED in approach check.

items.question: What should be done with the collective in hover landing?
options: Reduce collective gradually until touchdown, then fully reduce
items.explanation: Gradually reduce collective until touchdown, then fully reduce.

items.question: What is the required position of the cyclic during engine shutdown?
items.explanation: Shutdown calls for cyclic = neutral.

items.question: What is the required position of the collective during engine shutdown?
items.explanation: Collective must be locked during shutdown.

items.question: What is the position of the twist grip during engine shutdown?
items.explanation: Twist grip = IDLE during shutdown.

items.question: How long must engine oil cooling be maintained before shutdown?
items.explanation: Engine oil cooling: WAIT for 30 sec.

items.question: At what NR should rotor brake be applied in high wind conditions?
items.explanation: Apply rotor brake at NR <= 170 rpm in high wind, or NR <= 140 rpm in normal conditions.

items.question: What is the indication of a correct yaw load compensator check?
options: Right pedal moves forward without pilot input, or with low force
Both pedals are locked in place
items.explanation: During yaw load compensator check, right pedal moves forward without input or can be moved with low force.

items.question: What must be checked on the VEMD after shutdown?
options: Operating time, Ng/Nf cycles, and advisory messages
items.explanation: VEMD must show operating time, Ng/Nf cycles, and advisory 'FAILURE DETECTED' or 'OVERLIMIT DETECTED'.

items.question: What is the maximum fuel tank capacity of the AS350 B3?
items.explanation: Maximum capacity: 540 liters (142.7 US gal - 427 kg - 941 lb).

items.question: When does the unusable fuel quantity occur according to the fuel gauge?
options: When fuel gauge shows empty with caution light
items.explanation: The unusable fuel quantity is reached when zero is indicated on the fuel gauge.

items.question: Fuel quantity and flow indications are based on what fuel density?
items.explanation: Fuel quantity and flow indications are based on a density of 0.79 kg/l.

items.question: At the beginning of the yellow range on the fuel gauge, how much flight time remains at MCP?
items.explanation: 15 minutes of flight time remains at MCP at the beginning of the yellow range.

items.question: When operating in wind above 30 kt (56 km/h), how should the helicopter be parked?
options: With tail rotor facing the wind
items.explanation: The helicopter should be parked with the nose into the wind and rotor brake applied.

items.question: At what wind speed must the helicopter be tied down when parked?
items.explanation: For wind above 40 kt (74 km/h) the helicopter must be tied down.

items.question: During engine start in strong wind, what cyclic input should be applied?
items.explanation: When the rotor begins to turn, apply a small cyclic stick input into the wind.

items.question: During start-up in strong wind, at what Ng must the twist grip be set to FLIGHT?
items.explanation: As soon as Ng > 67 %, the twist grip must be set to FLIGHT.

items.question: What must be allowed during engine and rotor shutdown in high wind operations?
options: Engine oil to cool with twist grip in FLIGHT
items.explanation: Allow engine oil to cool with the twist grip in FLIGHT position.

items.question: Start up and shutdown have been demonstrated up to which wind condition?
items.explanation: Start up and shutdown have been demonstrated up to 40 kt from any direction.

items.question: What is the demonstrated limit for headwind during start-up and shutdown?
items.explanation: Start up and shutdown have been demonstrated for 50 kt headwind.

items.question: What must be monitored during cold weather start-up?
items.explanation: During cold weather start-up, engine oil temperature must be monitored.

items.question: What is the required engine oil temperature for cold weather start-up continuation?
items.explanation: Start-up continuation in cold weather requires engine oil temperature >= 0 °C.

items.question: Which CWP light must be checked during cold weather operation start-up?
items.explanation: During cold weather operation start-up, the CWP must be checked for ENG P.

items.question: Flight planning for the AS350 B3 must comply with which sections of the flight manual?
items.explanation: Section 4.1 states that flight planning must comply with limitations and performance in Sections 2, 5, 6 and supplements.

items.question: During the interior check, what is the required status of fuses or breakers?
items.explanation: The interior check requires that fuses or breakers are "All set".

items.question: During the interior check, what should be done with loads and objects carried in the cabin?
options: Placed on seats for easy access
items.explanation: Interior check requires all loads and objects carried to be stowed and secured.

items.question: Before starting the preflight check, what must be done with any picketing items (blanks, covers, blade socks)?
options: They may remain installed for protection
All picketing items must be removed
items.explanation: Section 4.2 states: 'Remove all picketing items if applicable' before the preflight check.

items.question: During the interior check, what must be verified about the fire extinguisher?
items.explanation: The interior check item is: 'Fire extinguisher - Secured - Checked'.

items.question: What cabin condition is required during the interior check?
options: Cabin free of loose objects but cleaning is optional
Cabin floor covered with protective mats
items.explanation: The interior check begins with 'Cabin - Clean'.

items.question: During engine prestart, what is the required status of the ICS and GPS navigation system?
items.explanation: Engine prestart checklist: 'ICS and GPS nav. system - ON'.

items.question: During engine prestart for night flight, how should the external electric mirror (if fitted) be set?
items.explanation: Prestart item: 'Electric mirror (if fitted) - SET to avoid dazzling (night flight)'.

items.question: What must be done with the [W/LT TEST] or [W/LT TST] switch during engine prestart?
items.explanation: Prestart checklist: '[W/LT TEST] or [W/LT TST] - PERFORM'.

items.question: When minimum engine oil temperature is reached during run-up, what should be done with the twist grip?
options: Cycle it between IDLE and FLIGHT
items.explanation: Run-up checklist: 'When minimum engine oil temperature is reached: Twist grip - FLIGHT position'.

items.question: Why must the collective be correctly locked before hydraulic accumulator and isolation checks?
options: To prevent main rotor blade droop on the ground
Because if not locked, the collective can move up when accumulators are depleted or the hydraulic cut-off switch is set to OFF
To reduce pilot workload during checks
items.explanation: The caution in the run-up section warns that if the collective is not locked, it will move up when accumulators are depleted or HYD cut-off is set to OFF.

items.question: How should the collective and cyclic friction locks be set before takeoff?
options: Fully released so controls move freely with no friction
Fully locked so controls cannot move
As required so that friction loads are felt when moving the flight controls
items.explanation: Before-takeoff checklist: 'Collective, cyclic friction locks - AS REQUIRED' with a note to feel friction loads when moving the controls.

items.question: What is the required landing light setting in the before-takeoff check?
items.explanation: Before-takeoff checklist: 'Landing light - AS REQUIRED'.

items.question: How does the recommended climb speed Vy vary with altitude in knots?
options: 65 kt at 0 Hp, increased 1 kt per 1000 ft
65 kt at 0 Hp, decreased 1 kt per 1000 ft
60 kt at 0 Hp, decreased 1 kt per 1000 ft
70 kt at 0 Hp, decreased 2 kt per 1000 ft
items.explanation: Section 4.5 gives Vy as IAS 65 kt at 0 Hp minus 1 kt per 1000 ft.

items.question: When operating in maximum power configuration, what is recommended before initiating a turn?
options: Increase collective slightly before the turn
Decrease collective slightly before the turn
items.explanation: Section 4.5 (Operation in maximum power configuration) calls for decreasing collective slightly before initiating a turn.

items.question: During the approach check, what must be done with all parameters?
options: Set them to maximum continuous rating
items.explanation: The approach checklist item is: 'All parameters - CHECK'.

items.question: During engine and rotor shutdown, what must be done with [PITOT], [HORN] and the landing light?
options: Leave them as configured in cruise
items.explanation: Shutdown checklist: '[PITOT], [HORN], landing light - OFF'.

items.question: At which rotor speed should [GEN] or [GENE] be switched OFF during shutdown?
options: When NR ≤ 170 rpm in high wind or NR ≤ 140 rpm in normal conditions
Only after the rotor has stopped
items.explanation: Section 4.6 calls for [GEN] or [GENE] OFF at NR ≤ 170 rpm (high wind) or NR ≤ 140 rpm (normal conditions).

items.question: Before leaving the helicopter after shutdown, what is stated regarding pitot, static ports, air intake and exhaust covers, and blade socks?
options: Fit or remove them as required
Only pitot and static ports may be covered
items.explanation: The shutdown checklist ends with 'Pitot, static ports, air intake and exhaust covers, blade socks as required'.

items.question: When parking in high wind, how must the rotor be positioned and secured?
options: Rotor brake released with blades free to weather-vane
Rotor brake applied with one blade at 12 o'clock and blade socks kept installed until start-up
Rotor brake applied with one blade at 3 o'clock
Rotor fully folded and tied to the tail boom
items.explanation: High wind operation: park head into wind, maintain rotor brake applied with one blade at 12 o'clock and keep blade socks until start-up.

items.question: During high-wind operations, how must the hydraulic checks in the run-up be performed?
options: With twist grip in IDLE and NR below nominal
With twist grip in FLIGHT position and NR at nominal speed
With engines stopped using battery power only
items.explanation: High wind operation run-up check: perform hydraulic checks with the twist grip in FLIGHT position and NR at nominal speed.

items.question: Which engine oil is recommended for low temperature operation?
items.explanation: The cold weather operation note recommends use of 3 cSt synthetic oil for low temperature operation.

items.question: In cold weather operation, what should be done with the twist grip once engine oil temperature is at or above 0 °C and ENG P has been checked on the CWP?
options: Keep the twist grip at IDLE
Move the twist grip to FLIGHT position
items.explanation: Cold weather start-up procedure: once engine oil temperature is ≥ 0 °C and ENG P is checked, set twist grip to FLIGHT position.
